name: What should I expect during a whole-house remodel inspection process?

mainEntity.name: How do inspections work during the different phases of a large remodel?
mainEntity.text: How do inspections work during the different phases of a large remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: The inspection process in a whole-house remodel is usually tied to construction milestones. Depending on scope, the project may be inspected after demolition, after framing, during rough electrical and plumbing, after HVAC rough-in, after insulation, and again at final completion. Each inspection verifies that the work meets code before the next stage is covered up. This process can affect the schedule because work may need to pause until an inspection is approved. If corrections are required, the contractor must address them before proceeding. That is why coordination between the construction team and the inspector matters so much. Homeowners should ask which inspections are expected and how delays are handled. Understanding the inspection sequence makes the timeline more predictable and reduces frustration when work pauses between phases. It also gives homeowners a clearer picture of where safety and code compliance are checked.
acceptedAnswer.description: Inspections usually happen at key milestones such as demolition, framing, rough electrical, rough plumbing, rough HVAC, insulation, and final completion. Passing each inspection is required before the next phase can continue.
